subject: Latent Programmer status: internal-DSL results + what the readout should say
body:
Hi Dmitri, Bruno,

Status rolling into the readout.

Reproduction closed in March: latent model beats the baseline Transformer on the released benchmark, consistent with the paper. On our internal transformation DSL (Ondrej's 40k-task dataset): top-1 synthesis accuracy 34% for the latent model vs 27% baseline, top-10 is 61% vs 52%. The latent codes are doing real work — inspection shows they cluster by transformation family (joins vs aggregations vs string ops), which also gives us a plausible UI hook: show the user the plan before the program.

The honest trade-off: at top-10, a user still has to pick among candidates, and 39% of tasks have no correct candidate at all. So the readout should pitch this as an assist with example-checking in the loop (we auto-run candidates against the user's examples and only surface ones that pass — that filter takes effective accuracy to 71% of tasks with at least one verified program).

Recommend scale-up: more data helps monotonically in our ablations, and the May 20 memo will size the Q3 ask against exactly that curve.

Efe
